state.seed_assertion: Systematic monitoring of the position/location of employees as well as of the content and of the metadata of employee communications, provided that it is fair and with the exception of logging files for security reasons, when the processing is limited to the absolutely necessary data and is specifically documented is a type of processing subject to DPIA requirement.

sentences.1: for example, a processing operation could evolve so that decisions are no longer automated or if a monitoring activity is no longer systematic, and the review of the risk analysis made can show that the performance of a DPIA is no longer required.
sentences.2: For example, a processing operation could evolve so that decisions are no longer automated or if a monitoring activity is no longer systematic.
sentences.3: When a supervisory authority's DPIA list involves processing activities related to the offering of goods and services to data subjects or to the monitoring of their behaviour in several Member States, or may substantially affect the free movement of personal data within the Union, it must be submitted to the consistency mechanism and must be communicated to the EDPB.
sentences.4: where the list involves"processing activities which are related to the offering of goods and services to data subjects or to the monitoring of their behaviour in several Member States, or may substantially affect the free movement of personal data within the Union", it must be submitted to the consistency mechanism and must be communicated to the EDPB
sentences.5: Systematic and extensive evaluation of personal aspects based on automated processing, including profiling, on which decisions are based that produce legal effects concerning the natural person or similarly significantly affect the natural person, is one type of processing that always requires a DPIA.
sentences.6: Article 35(3) sets out three types of processing which always require a DPIA: Systematic and extensive profiling with significant effects: "(a) any systematic and extensive evaluation of personal aspects relating to natural persons which is based on automated processing, including profiling, and on which decisions are based that produce legal effects concerning the natural person or similarly significantly affect the natural person."
sentences.7: The Data Protection Officer should monitor the performance of the DPIA.
sentences.8: The DPO should also monitor the performance of the DPIA (Article 39(1)(c)).
